decision: D1 — How does time organize the Checklist screen relative to the existing urgency buckets?
primary_axis: information hierarchy (what groups the list, what becomes a tag)
invariants: Same user: Mina, international student, Vancouver, arrived Aug 2026, stage 1
Same 11 Sanity tasks (international_student stage 1) and same 5 user-entered dates
Today fixed at 2026-09-03 in every phone
Tokens from constants/Theme.ts and constants/ChecklistPriority.ts; system font; 24/16/15/13 scale; 12pt cards; existing task sheet content (Why, Learn how)
Deadline sheet and add sheet are identical across options
Two scenarios rendered for each option: typical (week 4) and first open (no dates)
evidence: Can the user see what is due this week without scrolling, and does the screen still make sense on day one with no dates entered?

options.name: Timeline
options.bet: Time is the only grouping. Buckets become tags. Undated tasks sink to a 'No date yet' group with a Set a date prompt.
options.benefit: The next thing due is always first. Every task has a visible path to getting a date.
options.cost: The editorial structure (Do now → Optional) disappears from the top of the screen.
options.risk: On day one the screen is 11 undated tasks and a prompt, so it looks unfinished until the user adds dates.

options.name: Horizons
options.bet: Group by time horizon: This week, Next 30 days, Later. Undated tasks land in a horizon by their bucket.
options.benefit: Works on day one with no dates, and dated items slot into the same groups. Header answers 'this week'.
options.cost: The bucket-to-horizon rule is invisible; a Do now task looks due this week when nobody set a date.
options.risk: 'This week' can grow long for stage 0 users with many Do now tasks, pushing real deadlines down.

options.name: Dates board
options.bet: Deadlines are their own object: a horizontal board of countdown cards above the untouched bucket list. Only items due within 7 days are promoted into a 'Due this week' section.
options.benefit: Smallest change to what exists. Deadlines are visually distinct from editorial tasks, which is honest to the data.
options.cost: Two systems on one screen. Items due in 8 to 90 days live only on the board.
options.risk: Reads as a dashboard widget; with no dates it is one dashed card and the screen is today's screen.
